What works today

Oriel is a Customer 360 developer preview for one trusted local operator. This page records observed scope as of 10 October 2026. Start with the application quickstart. Authored sample definitions let you inspect a brief without a model or source credentials; context-agent bootstrap and questions require model consent.

Reproduce the checks

Install the committed connector dependencies, then run:

.venv/bin/python scripts/verify_customer360.py --timeout 300

This runs local gates only. The browser gate needs Node 22+ and an existing Chrome executable; the clean-install gate needs the locked dependencies in uv's offline cache. Missing prerequisites, skipped tests and missing suites fail verification rather than being counted as success. Reports and private receipts are retained under .oriel/verification/customer360/.

The default install helper records an isolated working-tree snapshot. A separate --require-clean-git run passed at 23:19 UTC on 9 October 2026 from a detached checkout of d8836a6ed8d0a34981b07dc7b87ca7ee08880e3f. It reconciled 313 copied public files plus its helper and workflow against committed blobs; the wheel contained all 308 package files, three UI assets and 25 sample JSON files. Both installed profiles passed before and after refresh with no model/vendor calls or dependency downloads. All 310 captured runtime, package-metadata and lockfile hashes match run g. See the exact command and limits. This is local Git provenance, not remote publication proof.

The command intentionally returns an incomplete overall result while required model or live gates remain unrun. Model and live flags select separately authorized checks; they do not grant access or provision credentials. See verification instructions.

The newer connector candidate also passed strict clean-Git installation at 23:48 UTC on 9 October 2026, from commit 6f4b0c664b00b57c59dd6494581c3cd7cbbf10c2 (tree 8fc2e13a35a16967e858c6a71dc8f1dabcfe6048). The checker reconciled 316 committed inputs, verified all 309 package files, three UI assets and 25 sample JSON files, then ran both installed profiles before and after refresh. It used no model calls, vendor calls or dependency downloads. The private receipt is clean-git-install-6f4b0c6/receipt.json, SHA256 470ac2ed4de133dd529ce009f2de2e72a78dc616f290b61904fe9f72bd3f3be7, under .oriel/verification/customer360/. This proves installation of the changed connector runtime from that local commit; it does not extend the earlier model result or prove public publication.

Existing advanced workflows

Local CSV/JSON/JSONL/Parquet imports, SQL, reviewed metric versions, read-only MCP stdio, local transformations and portable context bundles remain available. The CRM/product recipe demonstrates a separate consumer reusing a definition on changed data. These are useful independent features, not evidence of authenticated vendor compatibility or managed registry distribution.

The catalog includes 101 source definitions. Specific driver, resource and authentication combinations need their own checks. The connector guide and native verification record describe earlier runtime coverage. Gong is not currently a live catalog integration.

Remaining release evidence

  1. Publish the audited committed candidate and reproduce its documented experience from the intended public checkout. Local committed-source installation has passed; it cannot establish that the public repository contains this product revision.
  2. Run separately authorized live source combinations and an additional connector, recording exact resources, permissions, coverage and refresh behavior.
  3. Observe technical users completing an own-data customer review, then returning to reuse their context.
  4. Validate a receiving registry and consumer access when an actual sharing workflow requires them.

Comparative MCP/Rystic evaluations remain deferred. There is no qualifying accuracy, cost or latency advantage claim. Product plan · Roadmap · Evidence policy.
